endorsements.quote: Retain professional accountability and verify AI outputs against clinical and educational judgment.
Be transparent about AI assistance, avoid deception or manipulation, and disclose use in learning and care in line with policy.
Commit to ongoing, role-appropriate learning, resource training accordingly, and feed experience back to improve local policies and practice.
Embed equity in design and governance, ensure accessibility, use diverse data, and co-design with affected communities throughout development and evaluation.

unlisted_practices: Follow privacy, consent, and intellectual property requirements, and do not delegate legally reserved tasks to AI.
Check AI outputs for bias, report concerns, support auditing and updates, and adapt use as models and data change.
Use AI in ways proportionate to benefit and mindful of impacts on patient care, the workforce, and the environment.
Consider sustainability in AI procurement and oversight.
Treat AI as a present third party and choose words and uploads that protect relationships and trust.

screen.reason: This paper presents the development and validation of the Health CARE-AI consensus framework and principles for responsible AI governance/use via a modified Delphi study.
